history.summary: The 13th-century Surya (sun) temple at Ranakpur, adjacent to the famous Jain temple complex (about 350 m walk away). Built of white marble/limestone in Nagara style on a raised stone platform with no boundary walls, facing east; the octagonal mandapa before the sanctum and the walls, ceilings and pillars carry fine 'stone embroidery' carvings of warriors, horses and celestial bodies. It was destroyed at some point and rebuilt in the 15th century (per travel sources). Managed today by the Eklingji Trust. A large amphitheatre-like venue beside it hosts the Ranakpur Festival (verify).

name: Surya Temple, Ranakpur
town_description: Ranakpur is a village in Desuri tehsil of Pali district, in a forested Aravalli valley about 90 km from Udaipur. The Surya Narayan temple stands adjacent to the Jain temple complex; the nearby Amba Mata temple is also visited by devotees.
